chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, raising it regarding His, the Exalted, saying:
“I swear by this city; and you are a dweller in this city; and by a father and what he begot.”
He said: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and what he begot from the Imams عليهم السلام.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams عليهم السلام from his progeny
key_terms.الْبَلَدِ: the city by which Allah swears in the verse
key_terms.حِلٌّ: dwelling or residing lawfully in the city
key_terms.وَلَدَ: what was begotten or born from him

ai.seo_question: How is “وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ” interpreted in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This narration presents a tafsir of the verses by interpreting “a father and what he begot” as referring to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and the Imams عليهم السلام from his progeny. It highlights the wilayah-centered reading of the Qur’anic oath within Shia tradition and connects the verse to the line of divinely appointed leadership.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) raising it regarding the Words of the Exalted
[90:1] Indeed! I swear by this city [90:2] And you are a dweller of this city [90:3] And a father and what he begot.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and what he<sup>asws</sup> begot from the Imams<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah in a marfu‘ manner about the words of Allah, the Most High.
“I do not (need to) swear by this town (Mecca) [90:1] in which you are now living [90:2] or by the great father and his wonderful son . .” [90:3]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It refers to Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) and the Imams from his descendants.”
